- Treat confirmed media 401/403 responses as age-restricted content in profile grids and video playback.

issue.title: feat(dm): healthcheck NIP-44 capability at signer attach
issue.body:
## Summary

`useDmCapability` checked `Boolean(signer?.nip44)` — a type-presence test, not a capability test. A NIP-46 bunker that exposes the `nip44` API surface but rejects the underlying RPC produced sessions where DMs *appeared* available, every fetch silently failed, every send may fail late. This was the proximate failure mode behind #307.

This PR adds a one-time round-trip probe at session attach so the system fails-loud-at-the-boundary instead of fail-silent-deep-in-the-stack:

- New `probeBunkerNip44(signer, pubkey)` in `src/lib/dm.ts` — encrypt-to-self + decrypt-from-self with a small constant payload, returns `true` iff the round-trip plaintext matches the input.
- New `useBunkerDecryptHealthcheck()` hook — `useQuery` with `staleTime: Infinity, retry: 1, retryDelay: 1000`. Cached per `(signer, pubkey)` pair.
- `useDmCapability` gates `canUseDirectMessages` on the healthcheck result and exposes a new `isCheckingDmCapability` flag for loading-state rendering.
- `MessagesPage` and `ConversationPage` render a neutral "Checking signer capability…" surface during the probe instead of immediately showing the negative "DMs unavailable" copy.

## Motivation

Closes #311. Spun off from #307. The relay probe (separate work) confirmed gift wraps were on `relay.divine.video` for the moderator pubkey, ruling out propagation issues — the bunker decrypt path was the failure surface. This healthcheck catches that exact class of failure at the boundary, rather than letting it manifest as silent inbox emptiness.

Composes with #309 (surfacing decrypt failures): the healthcheck blocks the up-front promise of capability; #309 surfaces partial / runtime failures that occur after the healthcheck passes. Belt and suspenders.

## Trade-offs

- **Local-key signers (`NSecSigner`)**: round-trip is sub-ms — no perceivable change.
- **Bunker signers**: adds ~1× round-trip latency at first inbox load (~200–500ms typical for Keycast). Subsequent loads in the same session use the cached result. Acceptable for moderation/team accounts where capability assurance matters more than load time.
- **Stale-true is acceptable**: the healthcheck doesn't re-run mid-session. If the bunker recovers from a failed start, the user must reconnect to refresh the result. The runtime-failure surfacing in #309 catches the inverse case (bunker that probed OK but later fails).
- **Imperfect coverage**: probes self-encrypt + self-decrypt only. A bunker that grants self-decrypt but rejects ephemeral-key decrypt would pass this check but still fail real inbox reads — caught downstream by #309.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx vitest run` — 718/718 pass (added 5 probe tests + 3 healthcheck/capability tests)
- [x] `npx tsc -p tsconfig.app.json --noEmit` — clean
- [x] `npx eslint` — 0 errors
- [ ] Manual: requires a bunker that rejects nip44_decrypt to exercise the unhealthy branch end-to-end. The unit tests in `useDirectMessages.test.ts` cover all four states (probe pending, probe success, probe failure, no-nip44 short-circuit).

## Visual change

- `MessagesPage`: brief "Checking signer capability…" panel during the probe (typically <500ms for bunker users, sub-ms for local-key users).
- `ConversationPage`: same neutral panel during probe, then either the existing thread UI or a refreshed unavailable copy ("Your signer cannot complete a NIP-44 encryption round-trip. Try signing out and reconnecting your bunker.")

## Stacking

Independent of #312 (PR 1) and #313 (PR 2). All three branch from `main`. Order of merge is reviewer's choice; rebase on conflicts is straightforward.

issue.title: feat: family + age-review + kids — three sister pages for parents, teens, moderation, and policy
issue.body:
## Summary

Three sister static pages on the Divine apex, designed to be read together but each with a distinct audience and intent.

| Page | URL | Reader | Shape |
|---|---|---|---|
| Family resources | `divine.video/family` | Parents and guardians, conversation-first | Long-form guidance, anchor-nav, embedded STIR Lab interview |
| Account review | `divine.video/age-review` | Account holder whose account was just flagged | Short, deadline-shaped — 15-day window, two action paths, one no-response section |
| Kids policy | `divine.video/kids` | Curious parent, journalist, regulator, anyone looking up how Divine handles accounts for under-16s | Long-form FAQ explaining the under-13, 13–15, and 16+ tiers + the family-account carve-out + the policy stance |

The three are cross-linked:

- `/family` → `/kids` (for account policy specifics)
- `/age-review` → `/kids` (for context behind the rules)
- `/kids` → `/age-review` (for users with active reviews) and `/family` (for broader family guidance)

## divine.video/family — conversation-first guidance

Builds a polished static page at `/family` to support the in-app family-guide flow from the mobile app. Tone is direct, human, practical — conversation-first, not punitive or fear-based.

Covers, in order:

1. Hero — *"Safer social media use starts with conversation."*
2. Pause • Reflect • Redirect framing band
3. How to talk with your teen — co-navigate vs. surveil, respond before punishing, conversation starters
4. What Divine can and can't do — honest two-column ledger of moderation/reporting/support tools next to the things no app can guarantee
5. How content settings work — adult content gating, moderation lists, blocks/mutes, reporting
6. Feed habits and stopping points — habit framing, *not* "we eliminate infinite scroll"
7. Build a family media plan — collaborative, AAP-compatible
8. If your child saw something upsetting — pause → talk → tools → escalate
9. Rabble + Pam Wisniewski / STIR — embedded YouTube interview (lazy, `youtube-nocookie`) + STIR Lab links + pull quote
10. Trusted outside resources — Common Sense Media, AAP, HealthyChildren.org, ConnectSafely, FOSI, Thorn
11. Cross-link to `/kids` for account-rules specifics

## divine.video/age-review — the moderation action page

External page for accounts flagged in-app as possibly belonging to someone under 16. The reader is the flagged account holder, or a parent helping them resolve the review. Tight, deadline-forward, no policy ranting.

The 15-day window is the spine of the page. Sections:

1. Hero — *"Your account is under review"* + the 15-day window + suspension note + anchor nav
2. **Honest note for any under-13 reader** (placed before the action paths) — the account closes regardless because the rules around under-13 services tie our hands; the same person can create a new account when they're 13 or older
3. If you're 13 to 15 — two cards (what the video shows / how to send it) + privacy note + prefilled mailto to `support@divine.video`
4. If you're 16 or older and this is a mistake — single action card + prefilled mailto with the literal subject line *"I am 16 or older and think this account was flagged by mistake."*
5. What happens after 15 days with no response — orange card explaining closure + deletion mechanics; any email to support stops the clock
6. More context — single linked callout to `/kids`
7. Closing reassurance about re-emailing if no response

Body copy is ~620 words — reads in under a minute.

## divine.video/kids — the long-form policy page

Long-form FAQ-style policy explainer. The reader is a curious parent, journalist, regulator, or anyone trying to understand how Divine handles accounts for kids and teens.

Sections:

1. Hero — *"How accounts work for kids on Divine"* — explicitly routes flagged users to `/age-review` so they don't get stuck here
2. At a glance — three-card grid summarizing the under-13 / 13–15 / 16+ tiers
3. Why we work this way — policy stance (intrusive parent-verification critique, mass-data-collection critique, Big Tech moat point) + the 13–15 video as a different shape of consent check
4. Under-13 accounts — closure + deletion policy + parent-discovery action card with prefilled mailto + Nostr-relay caveat + come-back-as-a-new-account bridge
5. 13 to 15 accounts — video-requirement summary + linked callout to `/age-review` for active reviews
6. Families absolutely belong on Divine — the parent-held family-account carve-out (kids can appear in videos with their parent or guardian)
7. More family guidance — linked callout to `/family`

## Routing

- New routes: `/family`, `/age-review`, `/kids` on the apex — apex-only, no subdomain dispatch
- Per-page OG/Twitter meta on both Cloudflare Pages (`functions/[[path]].ts` via `serverSocialMeta.ts`) and Fastly (`compute-js/src/index.js` `handle*OgTags`), with crawler tests in `functions/[[path]].test.ts` for each apex path

## Copy refresh

Across `/family` and `/kids`, refer to Divine as an "app" not a "platform" — operational positioning the team uses going forward. The one academic-context exception is the STIR Lab research sentence, which says "online services" because that's the regulator-friendly term for the broader category their research covers.

## Brand / guardrails

- All three pages use `MarketingLayout`, `SectionHeader`, `Card variant="brand"` with accent shadows
- No `uppercase` classes, no gradients on layout surfaces, no `lucide-react` — Phosphor only
- Numbered lists across the new pages render as `font-extrabold` dark-green spans rather than native `::marker` (`::marker` font-weight is unreliable cross-browser); `aria-hidden` on the manual number spans preserves `<ol>` semantics for screen readers
- `tsc --noEmit`, ESLint, brand guardrail tests, and static-pages i18n test pass; production build succeeds; full suite is 138 files / 774 tests green

## Out of scope (intentional, needs follow-up)

- **Backend for the 15-day clock** — `/age-review` commits to behavior (signed Nostr-event notice delivery as the timestamp, account suspension during review, support's manual-close workflow at day 15, NIP-09 deletion request on closure) that the backend has yet to implement. Worth flagging to engineering before announcing the URLs.
- **Terms** — currently says *"may restrict or terminate."* Worth a one-line legal pass to acknowledge suspension as a real state alongside termination, now that the page commits publicly to it.
- **i18n** — all three pages are English-only on first landing. Locale JSON files + `useTranslation` + adding the new pages to `static-pages-i18n.test.tsx` are a single follow-up pass once stakeholders sign off on copy.

## Test plan

### /family

- [ ] Visit `/family` on the local dev server — verify hero, anchor nav, framing band, all 9 sections render
- [ ] Toggle dark mode — check hero, framing band, card accents, body copy all read well
- [ ] Scroll past ~600px — back-to-top button fades in bottom-right; clicking returns to top with smooth scroll
- [ ] Hover the resource cards (bottom of page) — chunky lift animation
- [ ] Lazy YouTube embed in the STIR section — 16:9, doesn't load until scrolled into view
- [ ] New cross-link card near the bottom — *"Looking for the account rules for kids and teens?"* — opens `/kids`

### /age-review

- [ ] Visit `/age-review` on the local dev server — verify hero (15-day window mentioned twice), anchor nav, all 4 main sections render
- [ ] **Honest note for under-13** is the first thing under the hero, before the 13–15 section
- [ ] 13–15 cards — bold readable numbers (not thin native markers); mailto button opens with prefilled subject + body to `support@divine.video`
- [ ] 16+ mistake card — same bold-number treatment; mailto button opens with the literal subject line in the brief
- [ ] "What happens after 15 days" section — orange card listing closure + deletion mechanics
- [ ] *"More context"* link card — opens `/kids`
- [ ] Slack/Twitter unfurl of `divine.video/age-review` shows the *"15-day window for responding"* description (crawler test in `functions/[[path]].test.ts` locks this in)

### /kids

- [ ] Visit `/kids` on the local dev server — verify hero, "this is the policy page, not the moderation page" callout (links to `/age-review`), and all 6 anchor sections render
- [ ] **At a glance** three-card grid — under-13 (violet), 13–15 (green), 16+ (blue) — readable in both light and dark mode
- [ ] **Why we work this way** card — the policy stance reads as intentional, not aggrieved
- [ ] Under-13 section — bold-numbered action steps; mailto opens with the parent-discovery prefilled body to `support@divine.video`
- [ ] Families absolutely belong on Divine — pink-accent card with the family-account carve-out
- [ ] Both linked callouts at the bottom resolve to the right pages (`/age-review`, `/family`)

issue.title: feat: family + age-review + kids — three sister pages for parents, teens, moderation, and policy
issue.body:
## Summary

Three sister static pages on the Divine apex, designed to be read together but each with a distinct audience and intent.

| Page | URL | Reader | Shape |
|---|---|---|---|
| Family resources | `divine.video/family` | Parents and guardians, conversation-first | Long-form guidance, anchor-nav, embedded STIR Lab interview |
| Account review | `divine.video/age-review` | Account holder whose account was just flagged | Short, deadline-shaped — 15-day window, two action paths, one no-response section |
| Kids policy | `divine.video/kids` | Curious parent, journalist, regulator, anyone looking up how Divine handles accounts for under-16s | Long-form FAQ explaining the under-13, 13–15, and 16+ tiers + the family-account carve-out + the policy stance |

The three are cross-linked:

- `/family` → `/kids` (for account policy specifics)
- `/age-review` → `/kids` (for context behind the rules)
- `/kids` → `/age-review` (for users with active reviews) and `/family` (for broader family guidance)

## divine.video/family — conversation-first guidance

Builds a polished static page at `/family` to support the in-app family-guide flow from the mobile app. Tone is direct, human, practical — conversation-first, not punitive or fear-based.

Covers, in order:

1. Hero — *"Safer social media use starts with conversation."*
2. Pause • Reflect • Redirect framing band
3. How to talk with your teen — co-navigate vs. surveil, respond before punishing, conversation starters
4. What Divine can and can't do — honest two-column ledger of moderation/reporting/support tools next to the things no app can guarantee
5. How content settings work — adult content gating, moderation lists, blocks/mutes, reporting
6. Feed habits and stopping points — habit framing, *not* "we eliminate infinite scroll"
7. Build a family media plan — collaborative, AAP-compatible
8. If your child saw something upsetting — pause → talk → tools → escalate
9. Rabble + Pam Wisniewski / STIR — embedded YouTube interview (lazy, `youtube-nocookie`) + STIR Lab links + pull quote
10. Trusted outside resources — Common Sense Media, AAP, HealthyChildren.org, ConnectSafely, FOSI, Thorn
11. Cross-link to `/kids` for account-rules specifics

## divine.video/age-review — the moderation action page

External page for accounts flagged in-app as possibly belonging to someone under 16. The reader is the flagged account holder, or a parent helping them resolve the review. Tight, deadline-forward, no policy ranting.

The 15-day window is the spine of the page. Sections:

1. Hero — *"Your account is under review"* + the 15-day window + suspension note + anchor nav
2. **Honest note for any under-13 reader** (placed before the action paths) — the account closes regardless because the rules around under-13 services tie our hands; the same person can create a new account when they're 13 or older
3. If you're 13 to 15 — two cards (what the video shows / how to send it) + privacy note + prefilled mailto to `support@divine.video`
4. If you're 16 or older and this is a mistake — single action card + prefilled mailto with the literal subject line *"I am 16 or older and think this account was flagged by mistake."*
5. What happens after 15 days with no response — orange card explaining closure + deletion mechanics; any email to support stops the clock
6. More context — single linked callout to `/kids`
7. Closing reassurance about re-emailing if no response

Body copy is ~620 words — reads in under a minute.

## divine.video/kids — the long-form policy page

Long-form FAQ-style policy explainer. The reader is a curious parent, journalist, regulator, or anyone trying to understand how Divine handles accounts for kids and teens.

Sections:

1. Hero — *"How accounts work for kids on Divine"* — explicitly routes flagged users to `/age-review` so they don't get stuck here
2. At a glance — three-card grid summarizing the under-13 / 13–15 / 16+ tiers
3. Why we work this way — policy stance (intrusive parent-verification critique, mass-data-collection critique, Big Tech moat point) + the 13–15 video as a different shape of consent check
4. Under-13 accounts — closure + deletion policy + parent-discovery action card with prefilled mailto + Nostr-relay caveat + come-back-as-a-new-account bridge
5. 13 to 15 accounts — video-requirement summary + linked callout to `/age-review` for active reviews
6. Families absolutely belong on Divine — the parent-held family-account carve-out (kids can appear in videos with their parent or guardian)
7. More family guidance — linked callout to `/family`

## Routing

- New routes: `/family`, `/age-review`, `/kids` on the apex — apex-only, no subdomain dispatch
- Per-page OG/Twitter meta on both Cloudflare Pages (`functions/[[path]].ts` via `serverSocialMeta.ts`) and Fastly (`compute-js/src/index.js` `handle*OgTags`), with crawler tests in `functions/[[path]].test.ts` for each apex path

## Copy refresh

Across `/family` and `/kids`, refer to Divine as an "app" not a "platform" — operational positioning the team uses going forward. The one academic-context exception is the STIR Lab research sentence, which says "online services" because that's the regulator-friendly term for the broader category their research covers.

## Brand / guardrails

- All three pages use `MarketingLayout`, `SectionHeader`, `Card variant="brand"` with accent shadows
- No `uppercase` classes, no gradients on layout surfaces, no `lucide-react` — Phosphor only
- Numbered lists across the new pages render as `font-extrabold` dark-green spans rather than native `::marker` (`::marker` font-weight is unreliable cross-browser); `aria-hidden` on the manual number spans preserves `<ol>` semantics for screen readers
- `tsc --noEmit`, ESLint, brand guardrail tests, and static-pages i18n test pass; production build succeeds; full suite is 138 files / 774 tests green

## Out of scope (intentional, needs follow-up)

- **Backend for the 15-day clock** — `/age-review` commits to behavior (signed Nostr-event notice delivery as the timestamp, account suspension during review, support's manual-close workflow at day 15, NIP-09 deletion request on closure) that the backend has yet to implement. Worth flagging to engineering before announcing the URLs.
- **Terms** — currently says *"may restrict or terminate."* Worth a one-line legal pass to acknowledge suspension as a real state alongside termination, now that the page commits publicly to it.
- **i18n** — all three pages are English-only on first landing. Locale JSON files + `useTranslation` + adding the new pages to `static-pages-i18n.test.tsx` are a single follow-up pass once stakeholders sign off on copy.

## Test plan

### /family

- [ ] Visit `/family` on the local dev server — verify hero, anchor nav, framing band, all 9 sections render
- [ ] Toggle dark mode — check hero, framing band, card accents, body copy all read well
- [ ] Scroll past ~600px — back-to-top button fades in bottom-right; clicking returns to top with smooth scroll
- [ ] Hover the resource cards (bottom of page) — chunky lift animation
- [ ] Lazy YouTube embed in the STIR section — 16:9, doesn't load until scrolled into view
- [ ] New cross-link card near the bottom — *"Looking for the account rules for kids and teens?"* — opens `/kids`

### /age-review

- [ ] Visit `/age-review` on the local dev server — verify hero (15-day window mentioned twice), anchor nav, all 4 main sections render
- [ ] **Honest note for under-13** is the first thing under the hero, before the 13–15 section
- [ ] 13–15 cards — bold readable numbers (not thin native markers); mailto button opens with prefilled subject + body to `support@divine.video`
- [ ] 16+ mistake card — same bold-number treatment; mailto button opens with the literal subject line in the brief
- [ ] "What happens after 15 days" section — orange card listing closure + deletion mechanics
- [ ] *"More context"* link card — opens `/kids`
- [ ] Slack/Twitter unfurl of `divine.video/age-review` shows the *"15-day window for responding"* description (crawler test in `functions/[[path]].test.ts` locks this in)

### /kids

- [ ] Visit `/kids` on the local dev server — verify hero, "this is the policy page, not the moderation page" callout (links to `/age-review`), and all 6 anchor sections render
- [ ] **At a glance** three-card grid — under-13 (violet), 13–15 (green), 16+ (blue) — readable in both light and dark mode
- [ ] **Why we work this way** card — the policy stance reads as intentional, not aggrieved
- [ ] Under-13 section — bold-numbered action steps; mailto opens with the parent-discovery prefilled body to `support@divine.video`
- [ ] Families absolutely belong on Divine — pink-accent card with the family-account carve-out

issue.title: fix(dm): NIP-17 self-wrap failure aborts entire send pipeline
issue.body:
Spun off from #307 — implementation step 2/3 of the moderator-inbox investigation.

## Problem

`createDmGiftWraps` in `src/lib/dm.ts` iterates `[sender, ...recipients]` and throws on the first sealing failure. The self iteration runs FIRST — so if `signer.nip44.encrypt(target=self)` rejects (or any other failure occurs in the self path), the loop bails before any recipient seal is even attempted. The recipient never receives the message.

Mobile's canonical implementation at `mobile/packages/dm_repository/lib/src/nip17_message_service.dart:114-132` does the inverse: recipient first, then self in its own try/catch with a "non-fatal" comment. That is the correct ordering — the self-wrap is a cross-device recovery copy; it must not be allowed to fail the primary path.

This is a latent fragility independent of #307's specific symptom. It's worth fixing for cross-client consistency and to remove a real failure mode from the send pipeline.

## Expected

Self-wrap failure logs a warning and is swallowed. Recipient delivery is preserved. Send mutation only rejects if the recipient path itself fails.

## Acceptance criteria

- New `createRecipientGiftWraps(input)` — sealing for recipients only; throws on failure.
- New `createSelfGiftWrap(input)` — best-effort; returns `NostrEvent | null`; logs `[DM] Self-wrap creation failed (non-fatal): <cause>` on rejection.
- `useDmSend.mutationFn` calls them in order: recipient first, publish, then attempt self-wrap. Self-wrap publish failure also swallowed with warn log.
- Existing `createDmGiftWraps` retained as a thin back-compat wrapper, marked `// TODO(#<this issue>): remove once all callers migrate` per `AGENTS.md`.
- Tests:
  - `dm.test.ts`: `createRecipientGiftWraps` produces N wraps; throws on encrypt failure. `createSelfGiftWrap` returns null and warns on failure.
  - `useDirectMessages.test.ts`: mutation resolves successfully when only self-wrap fails; rejects when recipient-wrap fails.

## Affected files

- `src/lib/dm.ts` — `createRecipientGiftWraps`, `createSelfGiftWrap`, back-compat wrapper
- `src/lib/dm.test.ts` — new test groups
- `src/hooks/useDirectMessages.ts` — `useDmSend.mutationFn` reorder + try/catch
- `src/hooks/useDirectMessages.test.ts` — mutation resolution semantics

## Out of scope

- Why a self-encrypt might fail (Keycast policy, transient bunker error, NIP-44 self-target rejection — orthogonal to this fix).
- Reading the self-wrap from relays (not a send-side concern).

## Risk

Behavior change: a flaky-bunker user who saw "Failed to send" today will see a successful send after this change (because the recipient genuinely did get the message). Correct, but a visible difference worth calling out in the PR body.

issue.title: feat(dm): healthcheck NIP-44 capability at signer attach

type.name: Feature
type.description: A request, idea, or new functionality

issue.body:
Spun off from #307 — implementation step 3/3 of the moderator-inbox investigation.

## Motivation

`useDmCapability` at `src/hooks/useDirectMessages.ts` checks `Boolean(signer?.nip44)` — type presence, not capability. A bunker that exposes the `nip44` API but rejects the underlying RPC produces a session where DMs *appear* available, every fetch silently fails, every send may fail late.

A one-time round-trip probe at signer attach time pre-validates the bunker. Combined with the surfacing work (separate issue), the system fails-loud-at-the-boundary instead of fail-silent-deep-in-the-stack.

## Design

- New `probeBunkerNip44(signer, pubkey)` pure async helper in `src/lib/dm.ts`. Runs `signer.nip44.encrypt(pubkey, '__divine_dm_probe__')` then `signer.nip44.decrypt(pubkey, ciphertext)`; returns `true` iff round-trip plaintext matches.
- New `useBunkerDecryptHealthcheck()` hook — `useQuery` with `staleTime: Infinity, retry: 1, retryDelay: 1000`. Cache key `['dm-healthcheck', pubkey]`. One probe per `(signer, pubkey)` pair, one retry on transient failure.
- `useDmCapability` reads the healthcheck result; `canUseDirectMessages = Boolean(user?.pubkey && signer?.nip44 && nip44Healthy)`.
- New `isCheckingDmCapability` exposed for loading-state rendering.
- `MessagesPage` shows skeleton during initial probe; falls through to existing `<DmUnavailableState />` (extracted shared component) when probe fails.

## Acceptance criteria

- Healthcheck runs at most twice per session per signer (initial + 1 retry).
- Local-key signers (`NSecSigner`) pass the healthcheck within 1ms (synchronous round-trip).
- Bunker signers add ~1× round-trip latency (~200–500ms typical) to first inbox load.
- When probe fails, `canUseDirectMessages = false`, no decrypt/send attempted.
- Tests cover: probe success, encrypt failure, decrypt failure, plaintext mismatch, no-nip44 short-circuit, retry-then-success, retry-then-fail.

## Affected files

- `src/lib/dm.ts` — `probeBunkerNip44`
- `src/lib/dm.test.ts` — 5 probe paths
- `src/hooks/useDirectMessages.ts` — `useBunkerDecryptHealthcheck`, `useDmCapability` gating
- `src/hooks/useDirectMessages.test.ts` — healthcheck retry; capability gating; loading state
- `src/pages/ConversationPage.tsx` — copy refresh in existing `!canUseDirectMessages` branch
- `src/pages/MessagesPage.tsx` — render skeleton during check
- New (shared with surfacing PR): `src/components/dm/DmUnavailableState.tsx`

## Out of scope

- Re-running healthcheck mid-session if the bunker recovers. Stale-true is acceptable; the surfacing work handles the inverse case.
- Probing operations beyond self-encrypt/self-decrypt. A bunker that grants self-decrypt but rejects ephemeral-key decrypt would pass this check but still fail real inbox reads — caught by the surfacing work downstream.

## Risk

Adds ~1× round-trip latency at signer attach for bunker users. Acceptable for moderation/team accounts where capability assurance matters more than load time. Local-key users see no change.

issue.title: feat(search): default to Hot sort and surface sort pills above results
issue.body:
## Summary

- The sort selector on `/search` was a small `<Select>` dropdown next to the search bar that users were missing. Promote it to a prominent pill row above the results, matching the Trending/Discovery feed pattern.
- Default sort changes from `relevance` to `hot` (recent + high engagement). Fresh `/search?q=X` URLs now land on lively videos instead of pure lexical-match order.
- URL canonicalization stays consistent: the default (`hot`) is omitted from the URL; any other mode (`relevance`, `top`, `rising`, `classic`, `controversial`) is written. Existing shared `?sort=top` links still resolve.

## ⚠️ Depends on funnelcake backend PR

This PR's sort pills change UI state and URL, but the **REST API silently ignores the `sort` param on `/api/search` and `/api/v2/search`** today. The backend fix is in: **divinevideo/divine-funnelcake#371**.

Evidence (same 3 IDs returned in same order regardless of sort value, on both prod and staging):
```
$ for s in trending loops engagement GARBAGE; do
    curl -s "https://api.divine.video/api/v2/search?q=dog&sort=$s&limit=3" \
      | jq -r '.data[] | "  id=\(.id[0:10]) loops=\(.loops)"'
  done
# all four produce identical output
```

OpenAPI confirms it: `/api/search` parameters are `tag, q, limit, offset, label, exclude_label, content_safety, nsfw, moderation_profile, type` — no `sort`. Root cause in funnelcake: `VIDEO_SORT_BY` hardcoded at `crates/api/src/search.rs:14`.

**Land funnelcake#371 first. Then this PR works end-to-end.** Until then, this PR is harmless — the param is just URL state and the existing hashtag/NIP-50 fallback paths already honor sort.

## What changed (web)

- `src/pages/SearchPage.tsx`: replaced `<Select>` + 6 imports with a `flex flex-wrap gap-2` button row reusing `SEARCH_SORT_MODES`, same icon set, brand-green tab styling from `TrendingPage`. Buttons accessible (`role="radio"` inside `role="radiogroup"`, `aria-checked`, `data-testid`).
- Default `useState` flipped from `'relevance'` to `'hot'`. Both URL writes (debounced sync + compilation-return path) gate on `sortMode !== 'hot'`.
- `src/pages/SearchPage.test.tsx`: 3 new tests cover default-hot initialization, `?sort=top` URL honoring, and round-trip URL write/erase on toggle.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx vitest run src/pages/SearchPage.test.tsx` — 17/17 passing
- [x] `npx vitest run tests/brand/` — brand guardrails clean
- [x] `npx vitest run` — 824/824 passing
- [x] `npx eslint src/pages/SearchPage.tsx src/pages/SearchPage.test.tsx` — 0 issues
- [ ] After funnelcake#371 deploys: live `curl https://api.divine.video/api/v2/search?q=dog&sort=loops` returns different ordering than `sort=trending`
- [ ] Visual: `/search?q=child&filter=videos`, confirm pill row above grid with Hot selected; click Top, verify URL `?sort=top` and grid re-sorts

issue.title: fix(dm): surface bunker decrypt failures in moderator inbox
issue.body:
Spun off from #307 — implementation step 1/3 of the moderator-inbox investigation.

## Problem

`unwrapDmGiftWrap` in `src/lib/dm.ts` collapses every failure mode (signer/bunker error, malformed seal, hash mismatch, recipient mismatch) into a single `null` return. `fetchDmMessages` then drops nulls without preserving any count. `useDmMessages.queryFn` returns the resulting `[]` as a successful query.

When a NIP-46 bunker (Keycast) cannot decrypt — transient timeout, missing `nip44_decrypt` permission grant, RPC rejection — the user sees an inbox indistinguishable from a genuinely empty one. No toast, no banner, no `query.error`. `MessagesPage` renders "No other messages yet" while the same account on `moderation.admin.divine.video` shows multiple established conversations (see screenshots in #307).

This violates the codebase rule that errors must surface, not silently disappear.

## Expected

The user can distinguish "system tried and failed" from "no one has DM'd me." When the entire fetched batch fails to decrypt, the inbox renders an explicit unavailable state rather than silently appearing empty.

## Acceptance criteria

- `unwrapDmGiftWrap` returns a discriminated union `DmUnwrapResult` instead of `DmRumorEvent | null`. Three branches:
  - `{ ok: true; rumor }`
  - `{ ok: false; reason: 'decrypt-failed'; cause: unknown }`
  - `{ ok: false; reason: 'malformed' }`
- `fetchDmMessages` returns `{ messages, fetchedCount, decryptFailures, malformedCount }`. Existing internal callers updated.
- `useDmMessages` returns the new shape; `useDmConversations` and `useDmConversation` read `data.messages`.
- New `useDmInboxStatus` derives `'ok' | 'empty' | 'unavailable'` from the meta. `'unavailable'` fires when `fetchedCount > 0 && decryptFailures === fetchedCount`.
- `MessagesPage` renders a distinct `<InboxUnavailableState />` when status is `'unavailable'`. Copy: signer needs to be reconnected.
- Tests in `src/lib/dm.test.ts`, `src/hooks/useDirectMessages.test.ts`, `src/pages/MessagesPage.test.tsx` cover each branch (TDD per `AGENTS.md`).

## Affected files

- `src/lib/dm.ts` — `unwrapDmGiftWrap`, `fetchDmMessages`, new `buildMessageFromRumor` extraction
- `src/lib/dm.test.ts` — branches for `DmUnwrapResult` + aggregate counts
- `src/hooks/useDirectMessages.ts` — cache shape migration; `useDmInboxStatus`
- `src/hooks/useDirectMessages.test.ts` — meta propagation; outbox merge still works after shape change
- `src/pages/MessagesPage.tsx` — 3-way status fork
- `src/pages/MessagesPage.test.tsx` — unavailable/empty/ok renders
- New: `src/components/dm/InboxUnavailableState.tsx`

## Out of scope

- Identifying *why* the bunker can't decrypt — covered by the healthcheck issue.
- Reducing concurrent unwrap pressure on the bunker — possible follow-up.
- Send-side fragility where self-wrap failure aborts recipient delivery — separate issue.

## Risk

Cache-shape migration in `useDmMessages`. Existing optimistic-insert tests must keep passing. Mitigation: write the cache-update helper before changing the queryFn return shape; run tests at each step.

issue.title: feat(dm): healthcheck NIP-44 capability at signer attach
issue.body:
## Summary

`useDmCapability` checked `Boolean(signer?.nip44)` — a type-presence test, not a capability test. A NIP-46 bunker that exposes the `nip44` API surface but rejects the underlying RPC produced sessions where DMs *appeared* available, every fetch silently failed, every send may fail late. This was the proximate failure mode behind #307.

This PR adds a one-time round-trip probe at session attach so the system fails-loud-at-the-boundary instead of fail-silent-deep-in-the-stack:

- New `probeBunkerNip44(signer, pubkey)` in `src/lib/dm.ts` — encrypt-to-self + decrypt-from-self with a small constant payload, returns `true` iff the round-trip plaintext matches the input.
- New `useBunkerDecryptHealthcheck()` hook — `useQuery` with `staleTime: Infinity, retry: 1, retryDelay: 1000`. Cached per `(signer, pubkey)` pair.
- `useDmCapability` gates `canUseDirectMessages` on the healthcheck result and exposes a new `isCheckingDmCapability` flag for loading-state rendering.
- `MessagesPage` and `ConversationPage` render a neutral "Checking signer capability…" surface during the probe instead of immediately showing the negative "DMs unavailable" copy.

## Motivation

Closes #311. Spun off from #307. The relay probe (separate work) confirmed gift wraps were on `relay.divine.video` for the moderator pubkey, ruling out propagation issues — the bunker decrypt path was the failure surface. This healthcheck catches that exact class of failure at the boundary, rather than letting it manifest as silent inbox emptiness.

Composes with #309 (surfacing decrypt failures): the healthcheck blocks the up-front promise of capability; #309 surfaces partial / runtime failures that occur after the healthcheck passes. Belt and suspenders.

## Trade-offs

- **Local-key signers (`NSecSigner`)**: round-trip is sub-ms — no perceivable change.
- **Bunker signers**: adds ~1× round-trip latency at first inbox load (~200–500ms typical for Keycast). Subsequent loads in the same session use the cached result. Acceptable for moderation/team accounts where capability assurance matters more than load time.
- **Stale-true is acceptable**: the healthcheck doesn't re-run mid-session. If the bunker recovers from a failed start, the user must reconnect to refresh the result. The runtime-failure surfacing in #309 catches the inverse case (bunker that probed OK but later fails).
- **Imperfect coverage**: probes self-encrypt + self-decrypt only. A bunker that grants self-decrypt but rejects ephemeral-key decrypt would pass this check but still fail real inbox reads — caught downstream by #309.

## Test plan

- [x] `npx vitest run` — 718/718 pass (added 5 probe tests + 3 healthcheck/capability tests)
- [x] `npx tsc -p tsconfig.app.json --noEmit` — clean
- [x] `npx eslint` — 0 errors
- [ ] Manual: requires a bunker that rejects nip44_decrypt to exercise the unhealthy branch end-to-end. The unit tests in `useDirectMessages.test.ts` cover all four states (probe pending, probe success, probe failure, no-nip44 short-circuit).

## Visual change

- `MessagesPage`: brief "Checking signer capability…" panel during the probe (typically <500ms for bunker users, sub-ms for local-key users).
- `ConversationPage`: same neutral panel during probe, then either the existing thread UI or a refreshed unavailable copy ("Your signer cannot complete a NIP-44 encryption round-trip. Try signing out and reconnecting your bunker.")

## Stacking

Independent of #312 (PR 1) and #313 (PR 2). All three branch from `main`. Order of merge is reviewer's choice; rebase on conflicts is straightforward.

comment.body:
Pushed `0004783` to address the review feedback.

**@DSanich** — good catch on the cache-staleness bug. Fixed by including the active `login.id` from `useNostrLogin()` in the healthcheck query key. `login.id` is a fresh UUID per `addLogin()` call, so a bunker disconnect + re-pair on the same pubkey now produces a fresh cache entry and re-runs the probe. No need for explicit `invalidateQueries` — the key itself differs. Added a regression test (`re-runs the probe when the active login id changes for the same pubkey`) that asserts the probe is called a second time after the login id flips.

**@mbradley** — thanks for the approval. On your two non-blocking points:

1. *Encrypt-to-self vs encrypt-to-other*: agreed — keeping encrypt-to-self for now since it matches the actual failure mode we're chasing (bunkers that reject all `nip44` RPCs uniformly). Happy to revisit if we ever observe a bunker that diverges between self and third-party encryption targets.
2. *Transient hiccup caching a false negative*: also agreed it's a known limitation. Worth noting that the new cache-key wiring (from the `@DSanich` fix above) widens the recovery surface a bit — a fresh sign-in now busts the stale `false`, not just a page reload. Still doesn't auto-recover within a single session without explicit user action, but the workaround is now "log out, log back in" instead of "hard reload".

Full suite: 719/719 ✓, `tsc` clean, `eslint` clean.

issue.title: feat: family + age-review + kids — three sister pages for parents, teens, moderation, and policy
issue.body:
## Summary

Three sister static pages on the Divine apex, designed to be read together but each with a distinct audience and intent.

| Page | URL | Reader | Shape |
|---|---|---|---|
| Family resources | `divine.video/family` | Parents and guardians, conversation-first | Long-form guidance, anchor-nav, embedded STIR Lab interview |
| Account review | `divine.video/age-review` | Account holder whose account was just flagged | Short, deadline-shaped — 15-day window, two action paths, one no-response section |
| Kids policy | `divine.video/kids` | Curious parent, journalist, regulator, anyone looking up how Divine handles accounts for under-16s | Long-form FAQ explaining the under-13, 13–15, and 16+ tiers + the family-account carve-out + the policy stance |

The three are cross-linked:

- `/family` → `/kids` (for account policy specifics)
- `/age-review` → `/kids` (for context behind the rules)
- `/kids` → `/age-review` (for users with active reviews) and `/family` (for broader family guidance)

## divine.video/family — conversation-first guidance

Builds a polished static page at `/family` to support the in-app family-guide flow from the mobile app. Tone is direct, human, practical — conversation-first, not punitive or fear-based.

Covers, in order:

1. Hero — *"Safer social media use starts with conversation."*
2. Pause • Reflect • Redirect framing band
3. How to talk with your teen — co-navigate vs. surveil, respond before punishing, conversation starters
4. What Divine can and can't do — honest two-column ledger of moderation/reporting/support tools next to the things no app can guarantee
5. How content settings work — adult content gating, moderation lists, blocks/mutes, reporting
6. Feed habits and stopping points — habit framing, *not* "we eliminate infinite scroll"
7. Build a family media plan — collaborative, AAP-compatible
8. If your child saw something upsetting — pause → talk → tools → escalate
9. Rabble + Pam Wisniewski / STIR — embedded YouTube interview (lazy, `youtube-nocookie`) + STIR Lab links + pull quote
10. Trusted outside resources — Common Sense Media, AAP, HealthyChildren.org, ConnectSafely, FOSI, Thorn
11. Cross-link to `/kids` for account-rules specifics

## divine.video/age-review — the moderation action page

External page for accounts flagged in-app as possibly belonging to someone under 16. The reader is the flagged account holder, or a parent helping them resolve the review. Tight, deadline-forward, no policy ranting.

The 15-day window is the spine of the page. Sections:

1. Hero — *"Your account is under review"* + the 15-day window + suspension note + anchor nav
2. **Honest note for any under-13 reader** (placed before the action paths) — the account closes regardless because the rules around under-13 services tie our hands; the same person can create a new account when they're 13 or older
3. If you're 13 to 15 — two cards (what the video shows / how to send it) + privacy note + prefilled mailto to `support@divine.video`
4. If you're 16 or older and this is a mistake — single action card + prefilled mailto with the literal subject line *"I am 16 or older and think this account was flagged by mistake."*
5. What happens after 15 days with no response — orange card explaining closure + deletion mechanics; any email to support stops the clock
6. More context — single linked callout to `/kids`
7. Closing reassurance about re-emailing if no response

Body copy is ~620 words — reads in under a minute.

## divine.video/kids — the long-form policy page

Long-form FAQ-style policy explainer. The reader is a curious parent, journalist, regulator, or anyone trying to understand how Divine handles accounts for kids and teens.

Sections:

1. Hero — *"How accounts work for kids on Divine"* — explicitly routes flagged users to `/age-review` so they don't get stuck here
2. At a glance — three-card grid summarizing the under-13 / 13–15 / 16+ tiers
3. Why we work this way — policy stance (intrusive parent-verification critique, mass-data-collection critique, Big Tech moat point) + the 13–15 video as a different shape of consent check
4. Under-13 accounts — closure + deletion policy + parent-discovery action card with prefilled mailto + Nostr-relay caveat + come-back-as-a-new-account bridge
5. 13 to 15 accounts — video-requirement summary + linked callout to `/age-review` for active reviews
6. Families absolutely belong on Divine — the parent-held family-account carve-out (kids can appear in videos with their parent or guardian)
7. More family guidance — linked callout to `/family`

## Routing

- New routes: `/family`, `/age-review`, `/kids` on the apex — apex-only, no subdomain dispatch
- Per-page OG/Twitter meta on both Cloudflare Pages (`functions/[[path]].ts` via `serverSocialMeta.ts`) and Fastly (`compute-js/src/index.js` `handle*OgTags`), with crawler tests in `functions/[[path]].test.ts` for each apex path

## Copy refresh

Across `/family` and `/kids`, refer to Divine as an "app" not a "platform" — operational positioning the team uses going forward. The one academic-context exception is the STIR Lab research sentence, which says "online services" because that's the regulator-friendly term for the broader category their research covers.

## Brand / guardrails

- All three pages use `MarketingLayout`, `SectionHeader`, `Card variant="brand"` with accent shadows
- No `uppercase` classes, no gradients on layout surfaces, no `lucide-react` — Phosphor only
- Numbered lists across the new pages render as `font-extrabold` dark-green spans rather than native `::marker` (`::marker` font-weight is unreliable cross-browser); `aria-hidden` on the manual number spans preserves `<ol>` semantics for screen readers
- `tsc --noEmit`, ESLint, brand guardrail tests, and static-pages i18n test pass; production build succeeds; full suite is 138 files / 774 tests green

## Out of scope (intentional, needs follow-up)

- **Backend for the 15-day clock** — `/age-review` commits to behavior (signed Nostr-event notice delivery as the timestamp, account suspension during review, support's manual-close workflow at day 15, NIP-09 deletion request on closure) that the backend has yet to implement. Worth flagging to engineering before announcing the URLs.
- **Terms** — currently says *"may restrict or terminate."* Worth a one-line legal pass to acknowledge suspension as a real state alongside termination, now that the page commits publicly to it.
- **i18n** — all three pages are English-only on first landing. Locale JSON files + `useTranslation` + adding the new pages to `static-pages-i18n.test.tsx` are a single follow-up pass once stakeholders sign off on copy.

## Test plan

### /family

- [ ] Visit `/family` on the local dev server — verify hero, anchor nav, framing band, all 9 sections render
- [ ] Toggle dark mode — check hero, framing band, card accents, body copy all read well
- [ ] Scroll past ~600px — back-to-top button fades in bottom-right; clicking returns to top with smooth scroll
- [ ] Hover the resource cards (bottom of page) — chunky lift animation

review.body:
lgtm — the probe design is sound for the actual failure mode we're seeing (bunkers that expose the nip44 api surface but reject the underlying rpc). two non-blocking discussion items:

1. the probe encrypts to self rather than to a third-party pubkey. for our current case (bunker rejects all nip44 rpcs) this is fine. if we ever see a bunker that handles encrypt-to-self differently than encrypt-to-other, we'd want to revisit, but that's theoretical for now.

2. `staleTime: Infinity` with `retry: 1` means a transient network hiccup at session attach would cache a false negative for the session. the query key includes pubkey so signer switches re-probe, and a page reload clears it. worth knowing as a known limitation but not worth complicating the caching for.

the loading skeleton is handled correctly — `canUseDirectMessages` is false during the probe so the compose button stays disabled and no "unavailable" flash. thanks, yet again, on behalf of support & t&s, @realmeylisdev. hope this review is sufficient to help get this over the line.

lgtm — the split into `createRecipientGiftWraps` (throws) and `createSelfGiftWrap` (returns null) is the right asymmetry. the null guard before `publishDmMessages` is correct, and the test coverage for both paths (self-wrap failure resolves, recipient failure rejects) is good.

thanks again on behalf of support & t&s, @realmeylisdev.

lgtm — clean separation between decrypt-failed and malformed, the `DmUnwrapResult` union follows the `InviteApiError.code` precedent nicely, and `useDmInboxStatus` is minimal and well-tested. TODO(#321) for the attestation sub-classification is the right call for scope.

one note: `docs/brainstorm/2026-05-02-pr-312-dm-decrypt-surface-review-brainstorm.md` is a useful analysis but AGENTS.md says "keep PRs tightly scoped to the task" — a 227-line design rationale doc is a process artifact, not a feature deliverable. recommend dropping it from this PR.

thanks for digging into this on behalf of support & t&s, @realmeylisdev.

Requesting changes before merge.

This PR is fine in principle, but it currently adds new report reasons without the companion serialization cleanup in `useModeration.ts`. Web still serializes raw enum values into the NIP-56 `e`/`p` tag type slot and the `NS-*` ontology label, so adding `child-safety` and `underage-user` widens existing protocol drift instead of actually aligning with mobile. Please keep this as one PR and add explicit mapping helpers in `useModeration.ts` for both the normalized NIP-56 type and the ontology label value, with test coverage for every `ContentFilterReason`.

The three new dropdown labels should also be normalized to sentence case to match the rest of `REPORT_REASON_LABELS` on web.
